classification.difficultyReason: Three given V-graphs of absolute-value functions, with one decision: a corner means not differentiable. No calculation is needed.

content.prompt: Decide whether these functions are differentiable at $x=2$.

answer.short: No. $f$ is continuous at $x=2$, but the gradients are $-5$ and $5$.
answer.worked:
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}-5(x-2),&x<2\\5(x-2),&x\geq2\end{cases}$$
Let $g(x)=-5(x-2)$ and $h(x)=5(x-2)$. First test continuity:
$$\begin{align*}g(2)&=0\\h(2)&=0\end{align*}$$
The branches join, so $f$ is continuous at $x=2$. Differentiate:
$$\begin{align*}g'(2)&=-5\\h'(2)&=5\end{align*}$$
The gradients differ, so $f$ is not differentiable at $x=2$.

answer.short: No. $f$ is continuous at $x=2$, but the gradients are $1$ and $-1$.
answer.worked:
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}x+1,&x<2\\5-x,&x\geq2\end{cases}$$
Let $g(x)=x+1$ and $h(x)=5-x$. First test continuity:
$$\begin{align*}g(2)&=3\\h(2)&=3\end{align*}$$
The branches join, so $f$ is continuous at $x=2$. Differentiate:
$$\begin{align*}g'(2)&=1\\h'(2)&=-1\end{align*}$$
